full_judgment:
Mr. M. H. Rahman, J: This appeal by leave, at the instance of the plaintiff, is directed against an order dated 7th June, 1990 passed in revision by the High Court Division, Dhaka upholding the order of the Court of appeal below rejecting the prayer for temporary injunction. 

 2. Appellant instituted O.C. Suit No.230 of 1988 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh against the respondents for a declaration that memo No.4166 dated 811 September, 1988 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh (respondent No.2) pursuant to an order of the Administrator of Waqf (respondent No.1) for her eviction form the suit premises was illegal and void and, further, for permanent injunction. His case, briefly, is that her husband, Bhola Mia was a monthly tenant under defendant No.3 and her brother Amir Emdad Khan since 1977, running a hotel business in the suit premises. Bhola Mia died on 1st  February, 1984, and since then plaintiff has been running the business and paying rent to defendant No.3, for her half share as per previous arrangement. Further case of the plaintiff is that her brother Amir Emdad Khan entered into an agreement with Bhola Mia on 28th January, 1980 allowing him to use his half share of the suit premises for 40 years, upon receipt of Tk.20,000/- as advance, fixing total rent Tk.36,000/-. Defendant No.3 gave out that she had purchased the share of Amir Emdad Khan. She serve a notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating the tenancy, but then filed an application to the Administrator of Waqf for eviction of the plaintiff on the ground that the plaintiff was in illegal possession of the suit premises which is a part of the Mohabali Khan Pathan Waqf Estate. 

 3. Defendant No.1 without any show cause notice to the plaintiff by a letter dated 21st July, 1988 asked the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh to evict the plaintiff, and the Deputy Commissioner in his turn issued the impugned memo. 

 4. Plaintiff prayed for temporary injunction which was opposed by defendants 1 and 3. That Bhola Mia was tenant in the suit premises was not denied, but it was alleged that after his death the plaintiff was never admitted as tenant and so she was a trespasser. 

 5. The suit on transfer to the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Mymensingh was renumbered as O.C. Suit No.10 of 1989. The Additional Assistant Judge by order dated 25th February, 1989 allowed the prayer for temporary injunction in respect of half of the suit premises. On Appeal by the plaintiff, the Additional Assistant Judge, by order dated 26th August, 1989 set aside the order of the Assistant Judge and rejected the application for temporary injunction. That order was upheld by the impugned judgment. 

 7. The respondents asserted that the suit is not maintainable against the Administrator of Waqfs, but failed to show whether the premises in question was at all a part of an enrolled Waqfs, None of the Courts considered the material question whether the Deputy Commissioner whose order of eviction has been challenged in the suit had at all any authority to issue such notice. The question is not whether the plaintiff is or is not a tenant in the suit premises but whether there is any prima facie ground for a eviction notice to be served upon her. The learned Advocate for the respondents failed to show any prima facie ground for the impugned notice. 

 8. The appeal is allowed with costs. The defendants are restrained from disturbing the plaintiff's possession in the entire suit premises till the disposal of the suit.
